title: The window opens straight into a rump lobe
summary: The chamber runs back into the rump as a lobe 15 mm wide, and the window in the left flank opens straight into that air: 253 mm^2 of chamber beside the jet, 5.7 times the window. The windway is a straight 30 mm slot through the tail and the lips stop 15 mm short of the window.

rejected.value: a window behind a throat (the print-first and character-first concepts)
rejected.why: window paths 15.8 and 17.0 mm long, 3.7 and 4.3 equal-area radii, outside every recipe in the acoustics notes: quiet and breathy by the panel's estimate; their designers' pitch models read high, and an independent solve gave 317 and 331 Hz against a designed 340 Hz

returns_if.text: when the chamber has to shrink below about 100 cm^3: a throat then works as a neck, if its junction is in the model and it is 7.5 mm wide or more

rejected.value: a long skewed windway to a 21 x 17 mm scoop on the flank (the acoustics-first concept)
rejected.why: the scoop lies where the thumb goes (64 cents flat with a pad resting over it) and a fingertip reaches the labium inside it; the 43.5 mm slot has about twice the length in which a string or a seam can sit; as drawn the concept failed the overhang evaluator (0.71 to 0.82 % against 0.5 %) and its print estimate was about 21 h and 107 g

returns_if.text: when a guard rib keeps fingers off the scoop and its roof is drawn again at 42 degrees: its pitch model was the only one of the three an independent solve confirmed

body: The lobe is the narrowest the design allows (250 mm^2 and 4.5 times the window). It was taken that narrow on purpose: the window's own conductance was 16 % too high for 340 Hz, and a narrower lobe lowers it without narrowing the jet. C9 holds it from becoming a throat again.
